title: SAP business partner: the partner, its roles, addresses and relationships, and the link from partner to customer and supplier (customer/vendor integration)
status_note: Every table, key and relationship below is taken from public documentation and written in our own words. None of it has been checked against an SAP system by this project; validate_plan checks it against your rows. A pack is a sourced suggestion, not proof.

variants.ecc: SAP ERP 6.0 (ECC): the business partner exists, but customers and suppliers need not be linked to it. Not verified per enhancement package.
variants.s4hana: SAP S/4HANA: customers and suppliers are maintained through the business partner, and the link tables are filled. Not verified per release.

tables.name: BUT000
tables.note: The client column is CLIENT, not MANDT. PARTNER_GUID is a second unique identifier, the one the link tables use. TYPE says person, organization or group.

tables.name: BUT100
tables.note: One row per role a partner has (customer, supplier, contact and others): a partner with three roles has three rows.

tables.name: BUT020
tables.note: A partner can have several addresses; the address itself is kept in the central address tables under ADDRNUMBER.

tables.name: BUT050
tables.note: Time-dependent: DATE_TO is in the key. RELTYP says the kind (contact person of, belongs to and so on), and the direction matters.

tables.name: CVI_CUST_LINK
tables.en: Link between business partner and customer
tables.note: One row per partner that is a customer. The partner is named by its GUID, not its number.

tables.name: CVI_VEND_LINK
tables.en: Link between business partner and supplier
tables.note: One row per partner that is a supplier. The partner is named by its GUID, not its number.

tables.name: ADRC
tables.note: Shared by customers, suppliers, company codes, business partners and document partners, through an address number. The key also has the start of validity (DATE_FROM) and the version (NATION: blank for the standard version, other values for the same address in another script, such as Latin and Kanji).

relationships.condition: Join on the GUID, never on PARTNER = CUSTOMER; both sides must carry the GUID in the same form.
Join on the GUID, never on PARTNER = VENDOR; both sides must carry the GUID in the same form.

ADRC's key also has DATE_FROM and NATION: take the standard version (NATION blank) and the row valid today. A join on the address number alone repeats the row once per version and period. Listed, not applied: neither filter is a fixed value the pack can apply (the blank may arrive as '' or ' ', and 'valid today' moves).

traps.title: The partner number is not the customer number
traps.text: A business partner and the customer or supplier behind it can have different numbers, depending on how number ranges were set up. Join BUT000 to KNA1 or LFA1 through CVI_CUST_LINK or CVI_VEND_LINK, never on PARTNER = KUNNR.

traps.title: The link tables use the partner's GUID
traps.text: CVI_CUST_LINK and CVI_VEND_LINK name the partner by PARTNER_GUID, a 16-byte identifier. Extraction tools may write it as binary, as 32 hex characters or as a dashed GUID; both sides of the join must come out in the same form.

traps.title: CLIENT, not MANDT
traps.text: The business partner tables call the client column CLIENT. The pack pairs it with MANDT of KNA1 and LFA1 explicitly.

traps.title: Roles multiply partners
traps.text: BUT100 has a row per role. Counting partners over a join with BUT100 counts a partner once per role; filter RLTYP to the role you mean.

traps.title: Partner relationships have validity and direction
traps.text: BUT050 carries DATE_TO in the key and two partners with a direction; pick the period, and read PARTNER1 and PARTNER2 by the relationship type.

traps.title: An address has versions and periods
traps.text: ADRC's key has the address number, the start of validity and the version (NATION). Joining customers or suppliers to ADRC on the number alone repeats them once per version and period: filter NATION to the standard version and pick the period valid on the date you report for.

traps.title: A document can carry its own address
traps.text: VBPA.ADRNR is filled when an order or delivery has an address of its own for a partner, such as a one-time ship-to address. Where it is empty, the partner's master address (KNA1.ADRNR) applies. Reports of where goods were shipped need the document address first.
